sports.h3: Cerundolo stuns Fritz from two sets down, Blockx dumps out Cobolli
sports.summary: Francisco Cerundolo came back from two sets down to beat ninth seed Taylor Fritz 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 on Arthur Ashe on Saturday, while Belgian 28th seed Alexander Blockx beat fifth seed Flavio Cobolli in four sets.
body: Argentine 24th seed Francisco Cerundolo ended Taylor Fritz's home run at the US Open on Saturday 5 September, rallying from two sets to love down for only the second time in his career to win 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 in three hours and 39 minutes. The turning point came at 3-4 in the fifth set, when he saved three break points from 0-40, then broke Fritz for the sixth time and served out the match. Fritz, the 2024 finalist, hit 54 unforced errors and suffered his earliest exit in New York since 2022.

Earlier on the same court Alexander Blockx of Belgium beat fifth seed Flavio Cobolli 6-7(4) 6-3 6-0 6-3, winning 11 games in a row from 2-3 in the second set. The 21-year-old fired 17 aces, reached the third round of a major for the first time and is the first Belgian man with a top-10 win at the US Open since 2000. Blockx, ranked 116 a year ago, now meets Cerundolo for a place in the quarter-finals.

sports.h3: Gauff cruises past Bucsa into US Open fourth round
sports.summary: Fourth seed Coco Gauff beat Cristina Bucsa 6-3 6-4 in 88 minutes on Saturday to stretch her winning streak to nine matches.
body: Coco Gauff needed just 88 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Saturday to beat Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3 6-4 and reach the last 16 in New York. The fourth seed closed it out when Bucsa's lob drifted long on match point.

Gauff arrived in New York after winning the Cincinnati warm-up and has now won nine matches in a row. She had needed a gritty three-setter to get past Paula Badosa in the second round. Her next opponent is either American teenager Iva Jovic or Alex Eala of the Philippines. Defending champions Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz had the day off and return on Sunday.

sports.h3: Keys blows 5-0 lead as Zheng and Potapova upset American seeds
sports.summary: Madison Keys lost 1-6 7-6 7-5 to Zheng Qinwen after leading 5-0 in the final set, and last year's finalist Amanda Anisimova went out 6-2 7-5 to Anastasia Potapova.
body: Saturday's third round produced two upsets on the women's side. Madison Keys, the 22nd seed, won the first set 6-1 in 23 minutes against Zheng Qinwen and led 5-0 in the decider before a run of forehand errors let the Chinese Olympic champion back in. Zheng, unseeded after elbow surgery kept her out of last year's tournament, won 1-6 7-6 7-5 for her second win over Keys this year.

Tenth seed Amanda Anisimova, who reached the final in New York in 2025 after beating Iga Swiatek and Naomi Osaka, lost 6-2 7-5 to 24th seed Anastasia Potapova. Mirra Andreeva advanced with a 6-2 7-6 win over Nikola Bartunkova.

sports.h3: Gasly takes shock maiden pole at Monza for Alpine
sports.summary: Pierre Gasly beat George Russell by 0.060s with a 1:21.786 in Q3 on Saturday, his first pole in ten seasons and Alpine's first since 2009.
body: Pierre Gasly produced the surprise of the 2026 season in qualifying at Monza on Saturday 5 September, lapping in 1:21.786 to beat Mercedes driver George Russell by 0.060s and McLaren's Oscar Piastri by 0.18s. It is the Frenchman's first pole in his tenth F1 season and the first for Alpine, in any guise, since Fernando Alonso for Renault in Hungary in 2009. Gasly won his only grand prix at the same circuit in 2020.

Gasly picked up a double tow behind the two Ferraris on his final lap, while Russell got stuck too close behind Max Verstappen and could not improve enough. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton qualified fourth and fifth for Ferrari, both within 0.008s of going out in Q2, with Verstappen sixth and reigning champion Lando Norris only ninth. Aston Martin qualified last for the seventh time in 13 races and Lance Stroll was knocked out in Q1 for the 100th time in his career.

sports.h3: Piastri drops to sixth after penalty, Antonelli starts from the back
sports.summary: Oscar Piastri was handed a three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson in Q2, promoting both Ferraris and Verstappen, while Kimi Antonelli starts last after a full engine change.
body: The stewards handed Oscar Piastri a three-place grid penalty on Saturday evening after ruling that his McLaren, which had just left the pits, held up Liam Lawson through the first chicane in the closing stages of Q2. Lawson missed the Q3 cut and vented on the radio. Piastri drops from third to sixth, which moves Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton onto the second row and Max Verstappen up to fifth.

Kimi Antonelli will start his home race from the back of the grid after Mercedes fitted a completely new power unit to his car. Twelve races in he had already used the maximum four internal combustion engines and exhausts and three energy stores. The 20-year-old, who qualified seventh, said he would attack from the start on Sunday.

sports.h3: PSV win heated topper 3-1 in Amsterdam, Ajax still winless at home
sports.summary: Ricardo Pepi, debutant Lutsharel Geertruida and Esmir Bajraktarevic scored as PSV beat Ajax 3-1 in the Johan Cruijff ArenA, in a match marred by a brawl after a Ruben van Bommel body check on Aaron Bouwman.
body: PSV took the first topper of the Eredivisie season on Saturday 5 September, winning 3-1 at Ajax. Ricardo Pepi headed in an Ivan Perisic cross after four minutes, Tolu Arokodare levelled in the 23rd minute and new signing Lutsharel Geertruida volleyed PSV back in front with the last kick of the first half. Steven Berghuis and Davy Klaassen both wasted big chances for Ajax in between.

The second half was dominated by a flashpoint when Ruben van Bommel caught Aaron Bouwman in the face with a body check and was only booked by referee Sander van der Eijk, sparking a melee that spilled onto the benches. Substitute Esmir Bajraktarevic sealed it in stoppage time. It was Michel's first defeat as Ajax coach and a fifth home league game without a win, leaving Ajax six points behind PSV with a game in hand.

sports.h3: Feyenoord up to second with 3-1 win at NEC before Barcelona trip
sports.summary: Gjivai Zechiel, Luciano Valente and debutant Jerayno Schaken scored in a second-half burst as Feyenoord won 3-1 in Nijmegen, with Anis Hadj Moussa left out for disciplinary reasons.
body: Feyenoord bounced back from last week's 2-2 draw with ADO Den Haag by beating NEC 3-1 at the Goffert on Saturday. All four goals came after the break: Gjivai Zechiel pounced on an Almugera Kabar error for his fourth league goal of the season, Darko Nejasmic replied with a fine left-footed strike from outside the box, then Zechiel set up Luciano Valente for 2-1 and debutant Jerayno Schaken added a late third.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst left winger Anis Hadj Moussa out of the squad after he turned up late twice, amid reported interest from Al-Ittihad. Feyenoord have 11 points from five games, nine of them earned away, and open their Champions League campaign at FC Barcelona on Wednesday.

sports.h3: Utrecht v Go Ahead Eagles abandoned after fireworks and thrown cups
sports.summary: The Eredivisie match at the Galgenwaard was stopped for good with Go Ahead Eagles leading 3-1 after repeated disturbances from the Bunnikside.
body: FC Utrecht's home match against Go Ahead Eagles on Saturday was abandoned after fireworks were thrown from the Bunnikside and cups landed on the pitch. The trouble began shortly after Victor Edvardsen made it 0-3 for the visitors in the 58th minute.

Referee halted play for more than 20 minutes before the teams came back out, but he sent both sides inside twice more, first for fireworks on the pitch and then for thrown cups. The game was then called off with Go Ahead leading 3-1. The KNVB will decide how the result is settled.

sports.h3: Spain and Australia dominate day one of SailGP Valencia
sports.summary: Diego Botin's Los Gallos won two of three Group B races on home water while Tom Slingsby's Flying Roos topped Group A on his 42nd birthday, as a dying breeze punished any slip.
body: SailGP's first visit to Valencia opened on Saturday 5 September with six races split across two groups in a breeze that faded to about 13 km/h by the end of the day. Spain's Los Gallos won Group B's first two races, the second by well under a second over Denmark's Rockwool Racing, before Nicolai Sehested's Danes led from the gun to take race three. Spain lead the group on 14 points from Denmark on 12 and the United States on 10.

In Group A, Australia's BONDS Flying Roos sit on 11 points after a win and two more top-four finishes, one ahead of Red Bull Italy, who won twice with Phil Robertson but scored zero in between. Artemis missed race one with a broken jib halyard yet recovered to two thirds. New Zealand's Black Foils finished sixth, fourth and sixth for just two points. Two more group races on Sunday decide who reaches the winner-takes-all final.

sports.h3: Malizia retakes Ocean Race Atlantic lead as MSIG Europe loses hours
sports.summary: Team Malizia leads United by the Ocean by 30.4 nautical miles, while Conrad Colman's crew spent two and a half hours on the bow fixing a snapped furling line in 30 knots.
body: Team Malizia has regained the lead in The Ocean Race Atlantic after losing it to United by the Ocean on day two, and now holds the biggest margin of the race so far at 30.4 nm. The German boat also won Friday's 20-minute Super Sprint, covering 12.02 nm, its second sprint win in three days.

MSIG Europe sits 175.1 nm off the lead after the furling line on its J2 headsail snapped in 28 to 30 knots, sending the sail flying and forcing skipper Conrad Colman and Elie Pirnay to reroute it by hand in the dark. DMG Mori lost a ballast tank hatch to slamming. With the fleet hard on the wind in squally conditions, organisers think the next few days could threaten the 24-hour record of 641.13 nm.

sports.h3: Master Worlds wraps in Las Vegas with black belt finals on Saturday
sports.summary: The IBJJF World Master Championship ran 3-5 September in Las Vegas, with brown and black belt divisions across all seven age groups on the mats and streaming on FloGrappling.
body: The 2026 IBJJF World Master Jiu-Jitsu Championship concluded on Saturday 5 September in Las Vegas after three days of competition. Brown and black belts across Master 1 through Master 7 competed on Thursday, with purple belt and further black belt brackets on Friday and the closing divisions on Saturday.

The event ran alongside the IBJJF Jiu-Jitsu Con International in the same venue. Full brackets and results are posted on the IBJJF database, and every mat was streamed live on FloGrappling. Next up on the grappling calendar is ADCC in Krakow on 12-13 September.

sports.h3: One week to ADCC Krakow: Duarte v Simoes for vacant superfight belt
sports.summary: With Gordon Ryan retired, the last two absolute champions Kaynan Duarte and Yuri Simoes headline ADCC 2026 at Tauron Arena on 12-13 September, with all 128 slots filled and men's purses doubled.
body: ADCC's biennial World Championship moves to Tauron Arena in Krakow, Poland next weekend, 12-13 September, the first edition outside the United States in years. The superfight title is vacant for the first time in 17 years after Gordon Ryan retired early in 2026, so 2024 absolute champion Kaynan Duarte faces 2022 absolute winner Yuri Simoes for the belt. Their last ADCC meeting, in 2019, ended when Simoes tore his ACL in the first round.

All 128 competitor places are confirmed, with six men's brackets of 16 and three women's brackets of eight. Total payout is $362,000, with men's division winners now earning $20,000 and the absolute and superfight winners $50,000 each, though women's purses still lag. The bracket reveal show is on Friday 11 September with the amateur worlds the same day.

consumer-tech.h3: IFA 2026 verdict: rollable Lenovo, bezel-free Tecno and Xiaomi's red fold
consumer-tech.summary: Gizmodo handed out its Best of IFA awards on Saturday as the Berlin show opened to the public, with Lenovo's Project Swan rollable laptop, Tecno's all-screen concept phone and the Xiaomi 18 Fold among the standouts.
body: IFA Berlin runs 4-8 September and the first public day on Saturday coincided with the awards round-ups. Gizmodo's picks included Lenovo's Project Swan concept, a 14-inch laptop with a flexible display hidden in the lid that unrolls sideways into a 17-inch ultrawide, plus the colourful IdeaPad Vibe with swappable keycaps. Tecno showed a fully working phone with no bezels at all, and Lexar's Muse SSD, which tapers from 3.8 mm to 1 mm and clips to an iPhone via MagSafe for ProRes recording, took the mobile accessory prize.

Xiaomi's 18 Fold sat behind glass in a bright red finish ahead of its launch next week. GSMArena noted the wide passport-style shape, a 5.38-inch cover screen, a 7.58-inch inner panel with a barely visible crease and Xiaomi's own XRING O3 chip. Belkin showed a slim power bank using semi-solid-state cells it claims last three times longer, and TechRadar's own list ran to 25 favourites including exoskeletons and somersaulting robots.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' event Wednesday: 18 Pro, iPhone Ultra and more
consumer-tech.summary: Apple's 9 September keynote at Apple Park is expected to bring the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the foldable iPhone Ultra, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 and AirPods 5, but no standard iPhone 18 until spring.
body: Apple's September event takes place on Wednesday 9 September at 10am Pacific at Apple Park. According to 9to5Mac and MacRumors, the lineup is three flagship phones, the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and the first foldable, expected to be called iPhone Ultra, plus Apple Watch Series 12 with a ceramic case option, Apple Watch Ultra 4 with new health sensors and AirPods 5 in versions with and without noise cancelling.

The base iPhone 18 is not expected until spring 2027, a break from the usual September cadence, and Engadget reports the cheaper models are likely to cost more because of surging RAM and chip prices. Apple will also confirm release dates for iOS 27, which includes a Passwords app feature that can change your passwords automatically.

consumer-tech.h3: Hands-on with Dyson's $499 CameraJet toothbrush at IFA
consumer-tech.summary: Dyson's first oral care product combines a brush, a water flosser and a camera that scans 28 frames a second to fire water between teeth, and Engadget tried it on a set of fake teeth.
body: Dyson's CameraJet was the headline of the company's ten-product unveiling around IFA, and Engadget got a demo on Friday, albeit on model teeth rather than its own. The $499 device pairs a brush head with a water jet that an onboard camera triggers as it passes each gap, analysing 28 live images a second. It went on sale on 1 September in the US, UK, France, Australia and Japan.

TechRadar has already reviewed it after a week of use and called it an effective if pricey solution, noting the camera doubles as a dental endoscope so you can see what you missed. Dyson also showed new robot vacuums, haircare devices and a very large air purifier at the same event.

consumer-tech.h3: Anker's SleepLab Pro speaker tracks your sleep with radar
consumer-tech.summary: The Soundcore SleepLab Pro uses a 60 GHz radar to log heart rate, breathing and sleep stages without a wearable, and learns which sounds and light settings actually put you to sleep.
body: Anker used IFA to show the Soundcore SleepLab Pro, a bedside speaker with a pop-up 60 GHz radar that monitors respiratory rate, heart rate and sleep stages from the nightstand. It plays soothing audio and dims a built-in light gradually, then records which combination worked so you can return to it.

Anker says the radar can distinguish you from a partner in the same bed. Gizmodo's reporters were sceptical about how contactless tracking compares with a ring or watch that infers sleep from body data. The speaker ships later this year and no price has been announced.

consumer-tech.h3: Sonos bets on Ace Ultra headphones and Beam Ultra soundbar
consumer-tech.summary: Sonos CEO Tom Conrad told TechRadar the $449 Ace Ultra and $699 Beam Ultra, on sale 29 September, are the start of a comeback after two years of software trouble.
body: Sonos announced the Ace Ultra headphones at $449 and the compact Beam Ultra soundbar at $699 on 1 September, with pre-orders open and shipping on 29 September. The Beam Ultra adds up-firing drivers for what Sonos calls true 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos in the same footprint as the old Beam, while the Ace Ultra gets a new driver, next-generation adaptive noise cancelling and a direct Wi-Fi link into the Sonos system.

In an interview published this weekend, Conrad said the new hardware runs on an AI-infused operating system spanning the whole Sonos range, with opt-in features including a ChatGPT tie-in. Reviewers still note the absence of DTS:X support.

consumer-tech.h3: NHTSA opens audit of Tesla Cybercab a day after Austin launch
consumer-tech.summary: Regulators want to see how Tesla self-certified a car with no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, in a query covering an estimated 1,000 vehicles opened the same day paid rides began.
body: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Audit Query AQ26002 on 3 September, the day Tesla started carrying passengers in the two-seat Cybercab in Austin. The filing says it was prompted by public information and covers about 1,000 vehicles. The agency is examining the technical basis on which Tesla declared the Cybercab compliant with federal safety standards, and specifically how far that relied on Tesla deciding certain standards do not apply to a car without human controls.

US automakers self-certify rather than get pre-approval, but many standards assume a wheel, pedals and mirrors. Tesla told NHTSA the car meets all applicable rules and that it will expand deployment gradually. The launch itself had no livestream or Musk remarks, with early riders reportedly signing NDAs. Tesla's FSD software is separately under an NHTSA probe covering 3.2 million vehicles.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla FSD v14.3.9 can now take the wheel from a human driver
consumer-tech.summary: A new active safety feature lets FSD Supervised engage on its own to steer around an imminent collision when braking is not enough, or when it thinks the driver is badly distracted.
body: Tesla's AI team said on Friday that FSD Supervised v14.3.9 is starting to roll out with a feature that activates without the driver's input when a crash looks imminent and automatic emergency braking alone may not prevent it. The system can take directional control and steer around an obstacle. It may also engage if the car judges the driver to be heavily distracted or FSD was disengaged by accident.

Until now FSD only ran when switched on. A slice of the v14 stack will now sit in the background during manual driving. Tesla has not said whether owners can disable it or how the car decides steering is safer than braking, questions Electrek raised given documented cases of v14 swerving unexpectedly.

consumer-tech.h3: VW plans 100,000 job cuts and may stop building EVs at four plants
consumer-tech.summary: Volkswagen's supervisory board approved its Future Plan 2030 on Thursday, adding 50,000 job cuts and leaving Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Audi Neckarsulm without new models after 2031 to 2034.
body: Volkswagen's supervisory board unanimously approved a sweeping cost plan on Thursday 3 September that calls for fewer workers, models, options, managers and investments as the group tries to catch up with faster-moving Chinese rivals. A further 50,000 positions will go worldwide, taking total planned reductions to around 100,000.

Four German sites, Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Audi's Neckarsulm plant, have no vehicle allocations lined up once current models run out at staggered dates between 2031 and 2034. VW said it cannot currently guarantee competitive production there, which could mean the end of EV assembly at those factories.

consumer-tech.h3: Ford targets 100,000 Fathom sales in the $30k truck's first year
consumer-tech.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Ford has set an internal goal that would make the sub-$30,000 electric pickup the best-selling non-Tesla EV in America when production starts in early 2027.
body: Ford wants to sell 100,000 of its upcoming Fathom electric pickup in its first year on sale, according to people cited by the Wall Street Journal. No automaker other than Tesla has moved more than 100,000 units of a single EV in a year in the US, so hitting the target would put the Fathom third in the national EV sales table.

The truck was developed at a skunkworks operation focused on cheaper manufacturing, uses a NACS charging port and is due to start production in the first quarter of 2027 at a price just under $30,000. Ford's previous electric pickup, the F-150 Lightning, launched well above its promised price and was eventually cancelled despite outselling the Cybertruck.

consumer-tech.h3: Rivian ships RivianOS 2 with Unreal Engine 5 and police alerts
consumer-tech.summary: Update 2026.31 puts every R1 and R2 on one software stack for the first time, with a rebuilt interface, real-time speed camera warnings and an AI layer called Unified Intelligence.
body: Rivian began rolling out RivianOS 2 on Friday 4 September, its biggest in-car software overhaul since the first R1 shipped. Version 2026.31 brings a redesigned interface, real-time 3D visualisations rendered in Unreal Engine 5 on the R2 and second-generation R1, plus live police and speed-camera alerts.

The update ends a period in which first-gen R1, second-gen R1 and R2 software had drifted apart. Hardware still sets limits, so original R1s stay on Unreal Engine 4 to keep performance up. Rivian has also confirmed lidar and an in-house chip for R2 advanced driving later in the year.

consumer-tech.h3: IKEA launches Liljebagge, its first Matter smart radiator thermostat
consumer-tech.summary: The Liljebagge fastens to a radiator and controls it via app or on-device buttons, with Matter and Thread support, at what TechRadar calls an impressively affordable price.
body: IKEA has added a smart radiator thermostat to its growing line of low-cost smart home gear. The Liljebagge attaches to a radiator valve and lets you set the temperature of each room independently through the connected app or buttons on the unit itself.

It supports Matter and Thread, so it works with Apple, Google and Amazon ecosystems as well as IKEA's own hub. International availability and pricing beyond the initial markets have not been confirmed, though TechRadar expects a worldwide rollout before the heating season.

consumer-tech.h3: Google Meet and Microsoft Teams rooms will finally talk to each other
consumer-tech.summary: Google's Workspace weekly recap for 4 September adds device interoperability between Meet and Teams hardware, plus admin audit logs for Gemini Notebook.
body: Google's Workspace Updates recap published on Friday 4 September introduces video conferencing device interoperability between Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, so meeting room hardware certified for one platform can join calls on the other without workarounds.

The same release gives Workspace administrators full audit logs for Gemini Notebook in the Admin console, showing how the AI notebook is used across an organisation. Both changes are aimed at large customers running mixed Google and Microsoft estates.
